manufacturer_data.description: Match manufacturer-specific AD data whose company ID + payload hex-decodes to ASCII "LEHUB1": either company 0x454C with payload prefix "HUB1" (hex 48554231, declared as the primary match; company 76 = 0x004C listed as the equivalent alternative reading with payload prefix "EHUB1"), or — most robustly — the ASCII substring "LEHUB1" anywhere in the raw AD structure. The LAST payload byte is a pairing-mode flag: 0x01 means the hub is in pairing mode and willing to connect; the vendor app hides hubs whose flag is not 0x01. Do not match on the local name — it is user-renamable over GATT and display-only.

Advertised manufacturer data spells ASCII "LEHUB1" when hex(company ID) and hex(payload) are concatenated, with a trailing pairing-mode flag byte (0x01 = pairing active). Split is ambiguous from static analysis: 0x454C+"HUB1" (declared here) or 0x004C+"EHUB1" — see discovery method description. MEDIUM confidence pending a real advertisement capture.

device.name: EmazingLights Spectra Smart Hub
device.notes:
EmazingLights Spectra is a programmable LED glove set. The phone does NOT talk to the gloves: it talks over BLE to a Spectra "Smart Hub" (firmware device type "PhotoHub"), which relays commands to the gloves over a proprietary 2.4 GHz link. A replacement client only needs the hub's BLE interface; the hub-to-glove RF link is out of scope (and out of reach of a phone). The hub is built on a Qualcomm CSR101x-family chip — its OTA service UUIDs are the documented Qualcomm CSR (uEnergy) firmware-update family.
ORPHAN STATUS: the app is delisted from Google Play, and the firmware manifest endpoint the app polls for OTA updates (http://www.facemeltcrew.com/ios/testmanifest.json) is DEAD — the domain no longer resolves (verified 2026-08-25, curl: could not resolve host). The app also has a cloud API for community features (glove-set upload/download/likes at gloving.com, plain HTTP with a hardcoded static app token) — it is NOT needed for control and is deliberately not reproduced here. All device control is local BLE.
DISCOVERY: the hub is found by MANUFACTURER-SPECIFIC advertisement data (AD type 0xFF), not by name. The vendor app's BLE scanner concatenates hex(2-byte company ID) + hex(payload minus its last byte) and requires the result to equal the ASCII string "LEHUB1" (hex 4c4548554231), plus the LAST payload byte to equal 0x01, which is a "pairing mode active" flag — a hub not in pairing mode does not appear in the app's scan results. The exact split is ambiguous from static analysis: either company ID 0x004C (unassigned test value) + payload "EHUB1"+flag, or company ID 0x454C + payload "HUB1"+flag (the discovery block below declares the second reading; both are MEDIUM confidence). A robust matcher scans the raw manufacturer AD structure for the ASCII substring "LEHUB1" and checks the trailing flag byte. The advertised NAME is user-renamable (see the housekeeping service) and is display-only — never filter on it.
COMMAND TRANSPORT: all commands are 20-byte frames written to the command characteristic (58511D0A-...) on the command service (F4DB6DA0-...):
  byte 0      header   = 0x55
  byte 1      opcode
  byte 2      index / param
  bytes 3-18  payload (16 bytes, zero-padded)
  byte 19     checksum = XOR of bytes 0..18
Frames are built as hex strings and written with a plain writeCharacteristic (default write type) — no bonding, no encryption, no authentication. The app contains no crypto at all. Command pacing during a sync upload is ONE FRAME EVERY 200 ms (the app's mode uploader sleeps 200 ms between writes); honour that pacing until live capture shows the hub tolerates faster.
OPCODE MAP (header 0x55 on all):
  0x01 writeModeSettings    payload [numColors, flashingPatternCode, 0,
                            motionType, 1, threshold, low, medium, high]
  0x02 writeBlockSettings   payload [blockIndex(1..n), R, G, B, 0, 1] —
                            one frame per color in the sequence
  0x03 changeDisplayMode    payload [mode]; app sends [1] after an upload
  0x04 changeRunMode        index=1, payload [0,0] = start running
  0x05 setPWMColor          payload [R, G, B] — direct color set
  0x07 flashingPattern      14-byte custom-pattern payload (only for
                            category-1/custom patterns; mode settings then
                            carry pattern code 0xFF)
  0x09 exitPairingMode      all-zero payload
  0x0A syncStarted          index 1 = sync start, 2 = sync end
Opcode 0x06 is skipped in the app (0x05 -> 0x07 gap) — likely reserved.
MODE UPLOAD SEQUENCE (what the app sends to push a mode to the hub):
  0x01 modeSettings
  -> N x 0x02 blockSettings (one per color; "M"/"L" brightness color modes
     are dimmed to 20% / 5% HSV value in-app before upload)
  -> optional 0x07 flashingPatternSettings (custom patterns only)
  -> 0x03 changeDisplayMode(1)
  -> 0x04 changeRunMode(index 1, payload 0,0)
The flashingPatternCode in mode settings is a small int enumerating classic built-in patterns (strobe/gap/repeat semantics); the code-to- pattern table lives in the app's bundled database and has NOT been extracted — see targets/emazinglights-spectra.md, remaining experiments.
OTA: firmware version is read from the housekeeping characteristic B66DAC3C-... (value parsed as a hex integer: high byte = major, low byte = minor). The OTA flow computes a CRC32 of the image zero-padded to a 16-byte multiple, then writes a 12-byte "new image" header [CRC32 LE 4B][image length LE 4B][00 10 01 08], sends syncStarted(start) on the command channel, and streams the image in 16-byte blocks over the CSR OTA characteristics, with a 10 s stall watchdog. Firmware binaries were hosted under the now-dead facemeltcrew.com root path; the manifest JSON schema was {"firmware":[{"deviceType":"PhotoHub","versionNum":N, "filename":"..."}]} with the binary at rootpath+filename.
CONFIDENCE: frame format, opcode map, service/characteristic UUIDs, the "LEHUB1" advertisement filter, 200 ms pacing and the OTA flow are HIGH (all read directly from the app's command builder and uploader). MEDIUM: the company-ID/payload split of the manufacturer data (needs one real advertisement capture); changeDisplayMode/changeRunMode operand semantics (values observed, meanings inferred); battery characteristic encoding (raw percent vs voltage unknown); whether the hub gates mode writes on the 0x09 exitPairingMode handshake; whether the command characteristic also notifies. LOW: factory reset behaviour (only indirect UI evidence that removing hub batteries is the recovery path).

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect while the hub advertises its pairing-mode flag and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state exists to clear — there is no bonding and no network configuration on the hub. The vendor's own recovery instruction for a wedged hub is to power it off or remove its batteries; stored modes and the user-set hub name may survive a power cycle (unverified).

steps.action: Turn the Smart Hub off, or remove its batteries for a few seconds, then power it back on.
steps.expect: Hub advertises again with the pairing-mode flag set and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: Power the hub, scan for the "LEHUB1" manufacturer-data marker with pairing flag 0x01, connect, and write command frames. No credentials are exchanged at any point.

steps.action: Power the Smart Hub and scan for manufacturer data containing ASCII 'LEHUB1' with trailing pairing-mode byte 0x01.
Connect and write 20-byte command frames to the command characteristic (58511D0A-...), paced at one frame per 200 ms during multi-frame uploads.
Send opcode 0x09 (exitPairingMode) when done pairing/syncing, mirroring the vendor app.

setup.notes: No provisioning, no account, no PIN, no bonding. The hub advertises with a pairing-mode flag in its manufacturer data; a central that finds the "LEHUB1" marker with flag 0x01 connects and writes 20-byte command frames directly. The app sends opcode 0x09 (exitPairingMode) when leaving pairing — whether the hub GATES mode writes on that handshake is unverified (MEDIUM); safest is to mirror the app: connect, run the upload sequence, then send exitPairingMode.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the hub to a phone or network, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old phone keeps auto-reconnecting and holding the link, remove the hub from that phone's OS Bluetooth list.

testing.notes: Everything here is static analysis of the delisted vendor Android app (com.emazinglights v1.8, versionCode 37). No live capture against real hardware has been replayed by this project.

change_display_mode.description: Opcode 0x03: switch what the hub displays; the app sends payload [1] ("show the just-uploaded mode") as the second-to-last frame of an upload. HIGH frame, MEDIUM operand meaning.

change_run_mode.description: Opcode 0x04: start running the uploaded mode. The app sends index=1 with payload [0,0] as the final frame of every upload; index=1 is presumed "run mode 1". HIGH frame, MEDIUM operand meaning.

set_pwm_color.description: Opcode 0x05: set a direct RGB color immediately (no mode upload). Payload [R, G, B]. HIGH.

sync_started.description: Opcode 0x0A: bracket a sync/OTA session — index 1 = start, 2 = end. Sent around the OTA image stream. HIGH.

write_block_settings.description: Opcode 0x02: one color block of the mode sequence — send one frame per color, in order, right after write_mode_settings. Payload [blockIndex(1..n), R, G, B, 0, 1]. The app dims RGB to 20% / 5% HSV value for its "M"/"L" brightness color modes before upload. HIGH.

write_exit_pairing_mode.description: Opcode 0x09: leave pairing mode; all-zero payload. The app sends this when leaving pairing — whether the hub requires it before accepting further mode writes is MEDIUM (unverified).

write_flashing_pattern_settings.description: Opcode 0x07: define a custom (category-1) flashing pattern; only sent when write_mode_settings carried pattern code 0xFF. 14-byte payload [strobeLen, gapLen, groupGapLen, brightnessSpeed, faderSpeed, colorRepeat, groupRepeat, groupingNumber, firstColorStrobeLen, firstColorGapLen, firstColorRepeat, firstColorPos, rampTargetLen, gapUpDown]. HIGH frame layout, MEDIUM field units/ranges (verify against live hardware).

write_mode_settings.description: Opcode 0x01: mode header for an upload — color count, built-in flashing pattern code (0xFF = custom pattern, followed by a 0x07 frame), motion-reactive settings. Payload [numColors, patternCode, 0, motionType, 1, threshold, low, medium, high]; the literal 0 and 1 are as the app emits them. threshold/low/medium/high are the motion-sensitivity band boundaries. HIGH frame, MEDIUM field semantics.

characteristics.name: Command
characteristics.notes: Write target for all commands AND the OTA image stream. Fixed 20-byte frames: [0x55][opcode][index][16-byte payload, zero-padded][XOR checksum over bytes 0..18]. Written with the default write type — no encryption, no authentication. Whether this characteristic also notifies is MEDIUM (unverified). Pace multi- frame uploads at one frame per 200 ms (the vendor app's uploader sleeps 200 ms between writes). All commands below are HIGH confidence from the app's frame builder; operand SEMANTICS flagged per command. Each template carries its trailing checksum as an auto-computed xor_checksum parameter over the whole preceding frame (checksum_start 0).

characteristics.name: Battery
characteristics.notes: Battery level, read-only. The app disconnects after two failed reads, so treat read failures as fatal to the session. Encoding (raw percent vs voltage) is MEDIUM — unverified; capture one read against a known charge state.

characteristics.name: Firmware Version
characteristics.notes: Hub firmware version, read-only. The app parses the value as a hex integer: high byte = major, low byte = minor (e.g. 0x0108 -> 1.8). HIGH. This is the version compared against the (now dead) OTA manifest's versionNum.

characteristics.name: Hub Name
characteristics.notes: User-facing hub name. Rename by writing the new name with each character encoded as its ASCII hex string (e.g. "HUB" -> "485542"). Display-only: the advertised name is never a discovery filter. Encoding HIGH (from the app's rename path); read-back format MEDIUM.

characteristics.name: OTA New Image
characteristics.notes: Receives the 12-byte new-image header [CRC32 LE 4B][image length LE 4B][00 10 01 08] before streaming. HIGH (CSR OTA family + app updater agree).

characteristics.name: OTA New Image Content
characteristics.notes: Image body, streamed in 16-byte blocks. HIGH.

characteristics.name: OTA Expected Sequence Number
characteristics.notes: Device-driven flow control for the block stream (CSR OTA expected sequence number). Property set MEDIUM — verify against hardware.

services.name: OTA Firmware Upgrade Service (Qualcomm CSR)
services.notes: The XXXXXXX0-8506-11E3-BAA7-0800200C9A66 UUID family with these prefixes is the documented Qualcomm CSR (uEnergy, CSR101x) OTA firmware-update service, which identifies the hub's chip family. OTA flow (from the app's firmware updater): CRC32 of the image zero-padded to a 16-byte multiple; write the 12-byte new-image header [CRC32 LE 4B][image length LE 4B][00 10 01 08]; send sync_started (phase 1) on the command characteristic; stream the image in 16-byte blocks through the new-image-content characteristic; abort on a 10 s stall. Firmware binaries were hosted under the now-dead facemeltcrew.com root — no image is currently obtainable from the vendor, so this surface is documented for completeness, not exercised.
